title: Remote state, locking and workspaces
scenario:
Your organization splits its infrastructure into two Terraform configurations. The platform team owns `platform/`, which manages the IAM role `app-runtime-role`, the instance profile `app-runtime-profile` and the S3 bucket `platform-artifacts`. It has been applied with local state, so nobody else can use it safely. The application team owns `app/`, which only contains a provider configuration so far, and needs one EC2 instance per environment that uses the platform's instance profile.

The S3 bucket `tfstate-lab` and the DynamoDB table `tf-locks` (partition key `LockID`) exist for remote state. Both configurations are in `/home/coder/lab`. The `aws` CLI is configured for the account and region `us-east-1`.

tasks.text:
Move the state of `platform/` to the S3 backend.

- Bucket `tfstate-lab`, key `platform/terraform.tfstate`, region `us-east-1`.
- State locking with the DynamoDB table `tf-locks` and encryption enabled.
- Nothing may be recreated.

Hint: add a `backend "s3"` block ([S3 backend](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/settings/backends/s3)) and run `terraform init -migrate-state`. Answer `yes` to copy the existing state, then delete the old local `terraform.tfstate`.
tasks.validation: Run `aws s3 ls s3://tfstate-lab/platform/`. The output should list `terraform.tfstate`, and `terraform plan` in `platform/` should report no changes.

tasks.text:
Create the application instance in `app/` with the platform's instance profile.

- Use the S3 backend with the key `app/terraform.tfstate` (same bucket, table and encryption as `platform/`).
- Read the platform outputs with a `terraform_remote_state` data source named `platform`.
- Create `aws_instance.app` (`t3.micro`, latest `amzn2-ami-hvm-*` AMI owned by `amazon`) with `iam_instance_profile` set from the remote state and the tag `Name = app-<workspace>` built from `terraform.workspace`.
- Apply in the `default` workspace.

Hint: see the [terraform_remote_state](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/state/remote-state-data) data source. Outputs are read as `data.terraform_remote_state.platform.outputs.<name>`.
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=app-default`. The output should show one running instance with the instance profile `app-runtime-profile`.

tasks.text:
Create the workspace `staging` for `app/` and apply there.

- `app-staging` must exist next to `app-default`.
- Each workspace keeps its own state.

Hint: `terraform workspace new staging`. The S3 backend stores other workspaces under `env:/<workspace>/<key>` ([workspaces](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/state/workspaces)).
tasks.validation: Run `aws s3 ls s3://tfstate-lab/env:/staging/app/`. The output should list `terraform.tfstate`, and an instance tagged `Name = app-staging` should be running.

tasks.text:
Migrate the state of `platform/` to the S3 backend.

- Bucket `tfstate-lab`, key `platform/terraform.tfstate`, region `us-east-1`.
- Lock the state with the DynamoDB table `tf-locks` and enable encryption.
- No resource may be recreated, and the local state must no longer hold any resources.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan` in `platform/`. The plan should report no changes, and `aws s3 ls s3://tfstate-lab/platform/` should list `terraform.tfstate`.

tasks.text:
Expose the data the application team needs from `platform/`.

- Add the outputs `instance_profile_name` (name of `aws_iam_instance_profile.app`) and `artifacts_bucket` (name of `aws_s3_bucket.artifacts`).
- The outputs must be readable from the remote state. No resource may change.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform output` in `platform/`. The output should show `instance_profile_name = "app-runtime-profile"` and `artifacts_bucket = "platform-artifacts"`.

tasks.text:
Create the application instance in `app/`.

- Use the S3 backend with the key `app/terraform.tfstate`, the same bucket and lock table, and encryption.
- Read the platform outputs with `data.terraform_remote_state.platform`. Do not hard-code the instance profile or bucket name.
- `aws_instance.app`: latest `amzn2-ami-hvm-*` AMI owned by `amazon`, `iam_instance_profile` from the remote state, tags `Name = app-<workspace>` and `ArtifactsBucket = <artifacts_bucket output>`.
- Apply in the `default` workspace.
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=app-default`. The output should show a running instance with the instance profile `app-runtime-profile` and the tag `ArtifactsBucket = platform-artifacts`.

tasks.text:
Deploy the application to the environments `staging` and `prod` with workspaces.

- Use the workspaces `staging` and `prod` of `app/`, each with its own state.
- `aws_instance.app` is `t3.small` in `prod` and `t3.micro` in every other workspace.
- `app-default` must keep running.
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=app-prod`. The output should show a running `t3.small` instance, and `terraform plan` in every workspace should report no changes.

expert.intro: `platform/` stores its state with the `local` backend in `platform/state/platform.tfstate`. A third, empty configuration `reports/` belongs to the reporting team.

tasks.text:
Migrate the state of `platform/` to the S3 backend with a partial backend configuration.

- Put `bucket = tfstate-lab`, `region = us-east-1`, `dynamodb_table = tf-locks` and `encrypt = true` into the file `backend.hcl` in the lab folder (next to `platform/` and `app/`) and pass it with `-backend-config`.
- The `backend "s3"` block in `platform/` may only set `key = platform/terraform.tfstate`.
- No resource may be recreated, and no local state file may hold resources anymore.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan` in `platform/`. The plan should report no changes, and `aws s3 ls s3://tfstate-lab/platform/` should list `terraform.tfstate`.

tasks.text:
Connect `app/` to the platform state.

- Add the outputs `instance_profile_name` and `artifacts_bucket` to `platform/` without changing any resource.
- `app/` uses the S3 backend with `backend.hcl`; its `backend` block only sets `key = app/terraform.tfstate` and `workspace_key_prefix = envs`.
- Read the outputs with `data.terraform_remote_state.platform`; do not hard-code the profile or bucket name.
- `app/` must work with the installed Terraform 1.6.6.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform init -backend-config=../backend.hcl` in `app/`. It should succeed, and `terraform console` should print `app-runtime-profile` for `data.terraform_remote_state.platform.outputs.instance_profile_name`.

tasks.text:
Deploy one instance per environment with the workspaces `staging` and `prod`.

- `aws_instance.app`: latest `amzn2-ami-hvm-*` AMI owned by `amazon`, `iam_instance_profile` from the remote state, tags `Name = app-<workspace>`, `Workspace = <workspace>` and `ArtifactsBucket = <artifacts_bucket output>`.
- `t3.small` in `prod`, `t3.micro` in `staging`.
- The `default` workspace must not manage any resource.
- The workspace states must be stored under `envs/<workspace>/app/terraform.tfstate`.
tasks.validation: Run `aws s3 ls s3://tfstate-lab/envs/ --recursive`. The output should list the states of `staging` and `prod`, and instances tagged `app-staging` (`t3.micro`) and `app-prod` (`t3.small`) should be running.

tasks.text:
The reporting team needs an inventory of the production instance, but must not get access to the application state.

- In `reports/`, create `aws_s3_object.inventory` in the bucket `platform-artifacts` with the key `inventory/prod.json`.
- Content: `jsonencode` of an object with `instance_id`, `instance_type` and `role_arn` (ARN of the role in the instance's instance profile).
- Look the values up with data sources by the tag `Name = app-prod`. Do not use `terraform_remote_state`, and do not hard-code IDs or ARNs.
tasks.validation: Run `aws s3 cp s3://platform-artifacts/inventory/prod.json -`. The output should show the ID and type of `app-prod` and the ARN of `app-runtime-role`.
